name: CanonicalWireframe Dependency Rules
purpose: Define how CanonicalWireframe interprets CCF Properties, Links, Events, Effects, causal relations, Link ownership/placement, Required Link satisfaction and flow.
principles: Canonical CCF structure remains authoritative.
NodeTypes define Entity-local Property expectations and mandatory Required Link declarations.
Rulesets define Property value semantics, Link interpretation, semantic roles, Link Property ownership/placement, flow and unresolved impact direction.
Required Link satisfaction is explicit canonical data through Link.value.required_link_ref.
Projection behavior is derived from resolved Ruleset semantics and is not canonical Ruleset state.
No semantics are inferred from filenames, extensions, names, paths, geometry, color or visual appearance.
Unresolved Ruleset or Required Link requirements produce unready state, not invalid canonical data unless declared canonical data itself is malformed or contradictory.
UNRESOLVED != INVALID

Event-to-Function implementation is represented by an explicit canonical event_handler Link from an Event Property to a Function Property; implementation binding is never inferred from function names, code proximity, filenames, decorators or rendering.

Function-to-Function invocation is represented by an explicit canonical function_call Link from the caller Function Property to the called Function Property; each Link represents one modeled call site and carries the call-specific canonical data surfaces through input_refs and output_refs.
Binding consumption is represented by an explicit canonical Link relation and never by free-text name lookup or transient visual trace lines.
Binding trace visualization may explain canonical routing but never defines canonical routing.
Forward and backward traversal through Binding follows canonical source and binding-consumption Links.
Abstraction inputs created by missing requirements are direct projections of concrete Required Link requirement instances.
Required Link input projection does not create an intermediate canonical Input Entity or boundary_input Link.
The external Abstraction input preserves the original required_link_ref identity and disappears when that requirement is satisfied.
Every readiness evaluation resolves against an explicit applicable specification version/set.
Historical satisfaction and current readiness are separate results.
Specification evolution changes evaluation context, not historical canonical truth.
Existing required_link_ref bindings are never silently rebound to superseding requirements.
A historical binding to a requirement absent from the current effective set contributes zero to current readiness without automatically invalidating the semantic Link.
Canonical readiness provenance is pinned by the canonical state/snapshot specification_ref, not supplied only as an external caller assumption.
A causal cycle may be valid; static causal traversal MUST terminate without mutating or guessing canonical semantics.
Specification provenance requires immutable reference resolution, not merely an immutable target artifact.
For preserved snapshots, the same specification_ref value must always resolve to the same specification-set content.
Mutable aliases and moving specification pointers are forbidden as readiness provenance.
The applicable specification set validates before the canonical model; specification failure and model failure are distinct result classes.
READY is a contract-conformance claim, not a claim that human intent or external reality is correct.
Free-text prose is never hidden semantic authority and cannot satisfy machine-readable requirements.
Validator implementation failure is reported as implementation failure, not converted into a semantic model result.
Semantic causal-cycle detection is path-scoped; convergence and fan-in are not cycles.
Validation contracts are version-scoped to the artifact being validated.
Later validation requirements are never applied retroactively to earlier valid artifacts.
Explicit migration is required to move an artifact under a newer validation contract.
Failure to resolve a required historical validation contract is an implementation failure, not a semantic model result.
Immutable specification provenance includes every transitive interpretation dependency, not only specification_ref.
Validation-contract dispatch must have immutable resolution: the same dispatch identity always selects the same contract content.
Local semantic refs resolve inside the pinned immutable closure; external interpretation refs require immutable resolution.
All Property/Ruleset semantic reference resolution is scoped to the canonical artifact's pinned immutable specification closure.
Historical ruleset_ref semantics are never reinterpreted through a newer/current Rulesets registry.
CW READY is a modeled contract-conformance claim, not proof of external implementation correspondence.
Artifact version identity, format version and specification_ref must form one coherent immutable interpretation context.
Version conflicts are explicit specification failures; validators never resolve them by precedence or latest-version guessing.
An unresolved Binding propagates UNRESOLVED through binding_consume to its consuming Output; Binding transport semantics are never considered resolved without a resolved Binding source.
Dependency derivation is declared directly on each governing Link Ruleset; prose alone never enables it.
Binding source scope and Binding consumer scope are both explicitly same-Abstraction-only.
Output has exactly one internal semantic source across boundary_output or binding_consume.
Specification integrity validation rejects dangling semantic mechanisms before model readiness evaluation.
Reference resolution never implies semantic target compatibility.
RULESET_API input_refs/output_refs are Entity-only and constrained to explicit I/O surface NodeType families.
RULESET_FUNCTION canonical refs remain intentionally broad by explicit policy rather than accidental omission.
Function logic MAY carry an explicit normalized operational representation through logic.representation_ref + logic.source.

Function logic is not required to be a byte-for-byte or line-for-line copy of original implementation source; it represents the function's modeled operation at the producer-selected abstraction level.

Function input/output semantics remain explicit through RULESET_FUNCTION input_refs/output_refs and function-to-function use remains explicit through function_call Links; consumers MUST NOT invent canonical I/O or call edges by parsing logic.source.
Function logic representation vocabulary is open; representation_ref identifies the notation/language used by logic.source, including values such as python, javascript, sql or hgi.

required_link_ref.meaning: Explicitly binds one canonical Link Property to one concrete Required Link requirement instance.

function_logic.meaning: Explicit normalized representation of a Function's modeled operational logic.
rules: representation_ref identifies the notation, language or representation used by source and is an open vocabulary.
source contains normalized functional behavior and is not required to reproduce the original implementation source verbatim.
The representation may omit implementation ceremony that does not change the modeled functional behavior.
logic does not replace canonical input_refs, output_refs, function_call Links, Event/Effect causality or other explicit canonical semantics.
Consumers MUST NOT create missing canonical references, call edges, data lineage or causal edges solely by parsing source.
Presence of logic does not by itself prove correspondence with an external implementation or runtime execution.

required_links.authority: NodeType.required_links declares the requirement; the canonical Link Property remains the relationship authority.
required_links.satisfaction_binding: A Link contributes to Required Link satisfaction only when value.required_link_ref identifies a concrete requirement that is effective in the applicable specification context and the Link matches that requirement's semantics.

authoring.zero_compatible_unsatisfied: Author the Link normally when otherwise valid; required_link_ref is absent.
authoring.one_compatible_unsatisfied: Structure may bind the newly authored Link automatically to that one requirement instance.
authoring.multiple_compatible_unsatisfied: User MUST explicitly choose exactly one compatible requirement instance before commit.

validation: required_link_ref.entity_ref resolves to the requiring Entity identity
if required_link_id is effective for that Entity in the applicable specification context, validate Link type, self_role, endpoint constraints and cardinality against that declaration
if required_link_id is not effective in the applicable specification context, preserve the binding but give it zero readiness contribution
one canonical Link is never reused to satisfy another concrete requirement instance
required_links.invalid: A required_link_ref is INVALID when malformed, when entity_ref is contradictory/unresolvable as canonical identity, or when it resolves an effective requirement in the applicable specification context but the Link contradicts that requirement's Link type, self_role or endpoint constraints. A previously valid binding is NOT invalid merely because its requirement is non-effective in a later specification version.
required_links.unready: A missing Required Link attachment leaves the requiring Entity UNRESOLVED/unready.

abstraction_input.projection: unsatisfied internal requirement projects directly as an Abstraction input
abstraction_input.satisfaction: A compatible external canonical Link authored through the projected input MUST carry value.required_link_ref pointing to the original internal requirement instance.

version_scoped_evaluation.current_effective_set: The applicable specification version defines which Required Link declarations are effective for the evaluation.
version_scoped_evaluation.historical_binding: A canonical Link may retain required_link_ref to a requirement that was effective in an earlier specification version.
version_scoped_evaluation.current_contribution: If that requirement is not effective in the current specification, the binding contributes zero to current readiness.
version_scoped_evaluation.link_semantic_validity: Non-effectiveness of the historical requirement does not by itself invalidate the underlying canonical Link relationship.
version_scoped_evaluation.new_requirement: A superseding/new Required Link is satisfied only by an explicit canonical Link bound to that new concrete requirement identity.

flow_patterns.name: Static
flow_patterns.meaning: The relation is semantically present but defines no transport leg.

flow_patterns.name: Call Return
flow_patterns.meaning: Caller invokes callee in parent_ref -> child_ref direction; modeled call output returns from callee toward caller.

target_ref.narrowing: A specific mount_type_ref contract MAY impose narrower target constraints; RULESET_MOUNT itself does not infer them.

readiness: every input_refs and output_refs item resolves when present
every resolved input_refs and output_refs item satisfies RULESET_FUNCTION reference_constraints
when logic is present, logic.representation_ref is present and is not an empty string
when logic is present, logic.source is present

input_refs.reason: Generic Function semantics may explicitly consume any canonical semantic endpoint.

output_refs.reason: Generic Function semantics may explicitly expose any canonical semantic endpoint.

logic_semantics.representation_ref_meaning: Identifies the notation/language/representation used to express logic.source; it does not have to equal the original implementation language.
logic_semantics.source_meaning: Human-readable or tool-consumable normalized operational logic for the Function.

readiness: filename is not an empty string
property_rulesets.rule: filename is the machine-significant external filename. Entity.name is display identity and MUST NOT substitute for filename.

readiness: every resolved input_refs item satisfies RULESET_API input_refs reference_constraints
every resolved output_refs item satisfies RULESET_API output_refs reference_constraints
property_rulesets.rule: api_type_ref defines the API kind; input_refs and output_refs define its canonical I/O surface Entities. Resolution alone is insufficient: each resolved ref must satisfy its side's explicit NodeType constraints. Additional API-specific settings belong in properties.

constraints: Each owned endpoint may have zero or one active ownership owner.
Assigning a new ownership owner replaces the previous active ownership relation.

boundary_semantics.transported_type: derived from parent_ref resolved canonical endpoint

scope_constraints: The internal source endpoint and Output Entity MUST belong to the same Abstraction semantic source.
Abstraction membership is canonical source membership and is never inferred from geometry.

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role cause_source
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role event
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

excluded_nodetype_refs.file_input: file_input declares a required external filename; it is not itself a parser/reader/data-flow source.

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role observed_source
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role event
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role input_source
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role event
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role event
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role output_target
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role event
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role effect
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role condition_source
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role event
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

implementation_semantics.meaning: The Function Property is the explicit implementation handler for the Event Property.
implementation_semantics.function_io_authority: The bound Function's RULESET_FUNCTION input_refs/output_refs remain the authority for its declared canonical I/O surfaces.

input_refs.meaning: Canonical Data Properties participating as caller-visible inputs at this specific modeled call site.

output_refs.meaning: Canonical Data Properties produced, returned or assigned as caller-visible outputs at this specific modeled call site.

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role called_function
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role caller_function
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

call_semantics.meaning: One function_call Link represents one statically modeled call site from one caller Function to one called Function.
call_semantics.input_refs: Call-site-specific canonical Data surfaces supplied to or read by the called Function for this invocation.
call_semantics.output_refs: Call-site-specific canonical Data surfaces produced, returned or assigned by this invocation.
call_semantics.source_mapper_rule: A source mapper may emit function_call and its input_refs/output_refs only from explicit source-level call and data-use evidence; name similarity, adjacency, rendering and inferred dataflow are forbidden.

dependency_derivation.dependency_target: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role effect
dependency_derivation.dependent: canonical owning Entity of endpoint in semantic role effect_target
dependency_derivation.unresolved_owner_result: UNRESOLVED; do not invent dependency endpoints

scope_constraints: Binding and consuming Output MUST belong to the same Abstraction semantic source.
The Binding's resolved canonical source endpoint MUST also belong to that same Abstraction semantic source.
Cross-Abstraction Binding source or Binding consumption is invalid.
Binding consumption is non-spatial; geometry never determines or limits the relation.

transported_semantics.type_signature: derived from the Binding resolved canonical source endpoint and its governing Ruleset

trace_semantics.forward: source endpoint -> canonical source Link -> Binding -> binding_consume -> Output -> downstream canonical route
trace_semantics.backward: downstream canonical route -> Output -> binding_consume -> Binding -> canonical source Link -> source endpoint

unresolved_semantics.origin: If the Binding is UNRESOLVED because its canonical source semantics are unresolved or absent, the Binding is the unresolved origin for this relation.
unresolved_semantics.propagation: UNRESOLVED propagates through binding_consume from semantic role 'binding' to semantic role 'binding_consumer'.
unresolved_semantics.consumer_effect: An Output consuming an unresolved Binding cannot derive a resolved transported semantic type/signature from that Binding and is therefore UNRESOLVED through this relation.

event_required_targets.rule: Event-related Required Link declarations may contain any number of independent mandatory targets.

event_read.effect_barrier: Event Effects become ready after all required reads for that Event have reached their Ruleset-defined ready condition.

derived_dependency.rule: A canonical Link derives an Entity-level dependency only when its own governing Link Ruleset contains dependency_derivation.dependency_forming=true.
evaluation: resolve the Link Ruleset from the pinned immutable specification closure
if dependency_derivation is absent or dependency_forming is not true, derive no dependency
resolve used_role and consumer_role against that Link Ruleset semantic_roles
resolve canonical owning Entity for each endpoint
if owners differ, used owner becomes dependency_target and consumer owner becomes dependent
if owners are equal, derive no Entity-level dependency
if an owner cannot be resolved, remain UNRESOLVED and do not invent dependency endpoints
derived_dependency.canonical_authority: The specific canonical semantic Link remains authority.

unresolved.rule: Unresolved impact propagates only from unresolved origin through each Link Ruleset's explicit unresolved_impact direction.
unresolved.required_link_origin: The requiring Entity is the unresolved origin when any concrete Required Link requirement is below min.

readiness.ready: All active Property, Link, Required Link and flow requirements are satisfied.
readiness.unready: One or more requirements are unresolved, missing or not yet satisfied.
invalid_examples: required_link_ref points to a requirement whose Link type, self role or endpoint constraints do not match the Link
declared Link property_owner cannot be resolved through the Ruleset semantic_roles
binding_consume references a Binding or Output outside the same Abstraction semantic source
binding_consume parent_ref does not resolve to an Entity of NodeType binding
binding_consume child_ref does not resolve to an Entity of NodeType output
required_link_ref has an invalid or contradictory requiring Entity identity
required_link_ref resolves an effective requirement in the applicable specification context but the Link contradicts its Link type, self_role or endpoint constraints
Binding has more than one active canonical source relation
Binding source endpoint belongs to another Abstraction or parent-level scope
Output has more than one active source relation across boundary_output and binding_consume
boundary_output or binding_consume crosses Abstraction source membership
readiness.principle: Unready structure remains canonical, visible and editable. UNRESOLVED != INVALID.
readiness.historical_rule: Historical readiness MUST use the historical specification context.
readiness.current_rule: Current readiness MUST use the current specification context.
readiness.superseded_required_binding: Preserved but contributes zero to current readiness.
readiness.historical_provenance_rule: Historical readiness cannot be reconstructed when the historical snapshot's specification_ref is missing or unresolvable; do not substitute current specification.
readiness.READY_scope: All applicable machine-readable readiness requirements are satisfied; no external-reality claim is implied.

authoring.link_type_resolution: Resolve valid Link Rulesets and endpoint roles from canonical context.

required_link_binding.zero_compatible_unsatisfied: Create ordinary valid Link with no required_link_ref.
required_link_binding.one_compatible_unsatisfied: May auto-bind to the one concrete requirement instance.
required_link_binding.multiple_compatible_unsatisfied: Require explicit user choice of exactly one concrete requirement instance before commit.

binding_consumption.selection_ui: Output may provide searchable Binding selection restricted to the same Abstraction.

abstraction_required_input.source: projected concrete Required Link requirement instance
abstraction_required_input.result: direct canonical Link creation carrying value.required_link_ref

function_call.input_refs: explicit canonical Data Properties evidenced at the call site; use [] when none are modeled
function_call.output_refs: explicit canonical Data Properties evidenced at the call site; use [] when none are modeled

input.cardinality: exactly one resolved incoming canonical semantic source at a time
input.typing: derived from the resolved source endpoint and governing Ruleset

source_relation_selector.candidate_rule: Binding child_ref must be allowed by the candidate Link Ruleset endpoint constraints.
source_relation_selector.search_scope: all canonical Links in the same Abstraction semantic source

input.source_owner_resolution: Entity endpoint -> that Entity; Property endpoint -> its canonical owning Entity.

output_consumption.multiplicity: any number of Outputs may consume one Binding
output_consumption.transported_semantics: derived from Binding resolved source semantics

trace.canonical_path: source endpoint -> source Link -> Binding -> binding_consume -> Output -> downstream route

abstraction_input_projection.source: unsatisfied concrete Required Link requirement instance
abstraction_input_projection.rendered_as: derived inbound socket/item on the parent Abstraction Entity
abstraction_input_projection.semantic_type: resolved from the Required Link declaration and governing Link Ruleset; never copied onto the projected socket

authoring.drag_to_input: Create the chosen valid canonical Link directly against the original internal requirement context and persist its value.required_link_ref.
authoring.multiple_compatible_required: If multiple projected requirements accept the same Link type, the user explicitly selects the concrete Required Link requirement instance being satisfied.

abstraction_input_projection.canonical_mutation: only the newly authored canonical Link is created; the projected input itself is not canonical data
abstraction_input_projection.resolved_transition: When the original Required Link minimum becomes satisfied, the corresponding unresolved input projection disappears.

specification_versioning.principle: Readiness is a result of canonical state evaluated under an explicit specification version/set.
evaluation_input: immutable specification-set artifact resolved by specification_ref

historical_evaluation.rule: Resolve the historical canonical snapshot's own specification_ref and evaluate against that immutable specification set.

current_evaluation.rule: Evaluate the current canonical state against the immutable specification set identified by its current specification_ref.

required_link_ref.identity: requiring Entity id + Required Link id
required_link_ref.explicit_migration_only: A migration may alter requirement bindings only if an explicit canonical migration operation is separately defined and performed.

specification_versioning.required_link_id_lineage_rule: Within one specification lineage, a Required Link id is a semantically immutable identity and MUST NOT be reused for a different requirement across specification versions.

provenance_binding.meaning: Pins the canonical state/snapshot to the immutable specification-set artifact that defines the applicable NodeTypes, Rulesets and inheritance context.

must_resolve: NodeTypes registry identity/content used by evaluation
Rulesets registry identity/content used by evaluation
inheritance semantics required for effective NodeType resolution
CCF/format/schema contract used to interpret each artifact
validation contract used to validate each artifact

link_validity_vs_requirement_satisfactio.semantic_link_validity: Validated independently against the Link Ruleset and canonical endpoints.
link_validity_vs_requirement_satisfactio.requirement_satisfaction: Evaluated only against effective Required Links in the applicable specification context.

forbidden: silent R1 -> R2 rebinding
silent mutation of L1
retroactive rewrite of T1 readiness
invented satisfaction of R2
evaluating T1 with SPEC_V2
collapsing historical satisfaction and current readiness
adversarial_requirement_mutation.provenance_rule: T1 and T3 are paired to their specification contexts by their own snapshot specification_ref values.

current.expected: R1 contributes 0; R2 unsatisfied; A UNREADY

id_reuse_case.forbidden: R1 removed in one version and later reintroduced with a different semantic meaning
id_reuse_case.required_action: allocate a new Required Link id

specification_provenance.purpose: Make the state-to-specification pairing explicit and reconstructable instead of relying on caller-supplied historical context.
specification_provenance.resolution: specification_ref MUST resolve exactly one immutable specification-set artifact.
specification_provenance.snapshot_rule: A preserved historical snapshot retains its original specification_ref. Changing the applicable specification requires an explicit state/snapshot evolution step.
specification_provenance.historical_readiness: Historical readiness is reconstructable only when both the historical canonical state and its pinned immutable specification set are available.
specification_provenance.missing_reference: If specification_ref is missing or unresolvable, historical readiness MUST NOT be invented; the result is UNRESOLVED/UNPROVABLE.
forbidden: substituting the current specification for a missing historical specification_ref
silently rewriting a preserved snapshot's specification_ref
placing specification version inside required_link_ref
inferring specification context from current registry contents

immutable_resolution.normative_rule: For the lifetime of a preserved canonical state/snapshot, identical specification_ref values MUST resolve to identical specification-set content.
allowed_identity_models: immutable artifact identity plus immutable version/revision
forbidden_reference_classes: any reference whose resolution may change over time without changing the reference value
immutable_resolution.syntax_requirement: Implementations MAY choose the concrete reference syntax, but MUST guarantee immutable resolution.

validation_contract_chain.validation_contract: immutable version-scoped contract selected by artifact version
validation_contract_chain.evaluation: performed only after artifact validation succeeds

causal_cycles.principle: A canonical causal cycle MAY be valid. Cyclicity alone does not make a model INVALID_MODEL or UNREADY.
causal_cycles.scope: CW causal tracing is static semantic graph traversal. It does not execute Events, Effects, state transitions, callbacks, retries or runtime loops.

traversal_state.definition: The canonical identity currently being traversed under the fixed trace direction (forward or backward) within one active traversal branch.
traversal_state.semantic_cycle_test: A cycle exists only when the same canonical traversal state is encountered again while that state is already present in the CURRENT ACTIVE TRAVERSAL PATH.

termination.rule: When a traversal state already present in the current active path is encountered, record the cycle closure and stop recursively expanding THAT ROUTE beyond the repeated state.

causal_cycles.unresolved_propagation: UNRESOLVED propagation through a valid causal cycle follows declared impact directions. Cycle closure is detected path-scopingly; the affected route terminates at closure without repeated expansion or semantic mutation.
forbidden: classifying a node as cyclic merely because it was reached earlier in another branch
using a trace-global visited set as semantic cycle authority
deleting or ignoring canonical edges merely to guarantee termination
inventing a missing edge or cycle break
inferring runtime repetition count from a causal cycle
treating static graph traversal as Event execution

expected.closure_at: A when A is encountered while already in current active path

causal_cycle_test_oracle.rule: Reaching the same canonical identity through another completed/parallel branch is not sufficient for cycle classification.

specification_reference_validation.valid: specification_ref resolves exactly one immutable specification-set artifact and the resolution is immutable: the same reference value always resolves to the same content.
invalid: specification_ref resolves through a mutable alias or moving pointer
the same specification_ref value can resolve to different specification-set content over time
specification_ref target is mutable under the same identity
specification_reference_validation.historical_reconstruction: Historical readiness is reconstructable only when the historical snapshot carries a specification_ref whose resolution is immutable and whose referenced specification-set artifact remains available.

invalid_scenario.T1: snapshot.specification_ref = CURRENT_SPEC; CURRENT_SPEC resolves to SPEC_V1
invalid_scenario.T3: same snapshot.specification_ref = CURRENT_SPEC; CURRENT_SPEC now resolves to SPEC_V2

adversarial_mutable_specification_ref.expected: This provenance mechanism is invalid because identical specification_ref values do not have immutable resolution.
adversarial_mutable_specification_ref.forbidden_fix: Do not infer that the historical snapshot used SPEC_V1 merely from external history.
adversarial_mutable_specification_ref.required_property: same specification_ref value -> same specification-set content for the lifetime of the preserved snapshot

classes.INVALID_SPECIFICATION: The applicable specification set (NodeTypes, Rulesets, inheritance or their internal references/constraints) is contradictory, malformed, ambiguous or otherwise invalid.
classes.INVALID_MODEL: The applicable specification set is valid, but declared canonical model data violates it or is itself malformed/contradictory.
classes.UNREADY: Specification and canonical model are valid, but one or more declared readiness requirements are not currently satisfied.
classes.READY: Specification and canonical model are valid and all applicable machine-readable readiness requirements are satisfied.
classes.IMPLEMENTATION_FAILURE: The validator/runtime failed to execute the specification correctly, for example because of a crash, race condition, non-termination, resource exhaustion or internal defect.

rules: INVALID_SPECIFICATION aborts canonical model readiness evaluation.
INVALID_MODEL is reported only after the applicable specification set itself is valid.
READY is not a claim of real-world correctness.
IMPLEMENTATION_FAILURE is not converted into READY, UNREADY, INVALID_MODEL or INVALID_SPECIFICATION.
evaluation_result_model.historical_contract_resolution: Failure to resolve a required historical validation contract is IMPLEMENTATION_FAILURE, not INVALID_SPECIFICATION and not INVALID_MODEL.

specification_self_validation.validation_contract_selection: Each specification artifact is self-validated under the validation contract selected by its own declared format/schema version.

prose_semantics_boundary.principle: Free-text prose is non-authoritative for machine validation unless a separate contract explicitly defines a structured field as semantic input. Ordinary summary/notes/comment text is never semantic authority.
cannot: change a Link type or semantic role
prose_semantics_boundary.formalization_requirement: Architectural constraints that must affect machine behavior MUST be moved into structured canonical semantics governed by NodeTypes/Rulesets.

model_claim_boundary.READY_claim: The canonical model is valid and satisfies all machine-readable readiness requirements under its pinned valid specification context.
model_claim_boundary.external_truth_validation: outside CW unless explicitly modeled through additional contracts/evidence

validator_implementation_conformance.principle: The specification defines required semantic behavior; a concrete validator implementation that fails to produce that behavior is non-conformant.
requirements: deterministic interpretation of the same canonical state + same specification_ref
no data races that change semantic results
no silent fallback after internal failure
resource failure must not be misreported as semantic validity/readiness
version-aware validation-contract dispatch before artifact validation
historical artifacts are validated with their own applicable validation contract
no silent latest-version fallback when a historical validation contract is required

validation_contract_versioning.principle: Every specification artifact is validated under the validation contract applicable to that artifact's own declared format/schema version.
dispatch_order: read artifact-declared validation/format identity and version
resolve exactly one immutable validation-contract content through an immutable dispatch mapping/reference
validate the artifact using that contract
only then use the validated artifact in model evaluation

historical_artifacts.missing_later_field: A historical artifact is not invalid merely because it lacks a field introduced as mandatory only in a later validation contract.

current_artifacts.rule: A current artifact MUST satisfy every requirement of its own applicable current validation contract.

migration.result: Migration produces a new artifact governed by the target validation contract; it does not rewrite the historical artifact.

historical_valid.expected: SPEC_V1 is not invalid merely for lacking that later field.

forbidden: validate SPEC_V1 using VALIDATION_CONTRACT_V3 merely because V3 is latest
retroactively mutate SPEC_V1
silently inject missing later fields
implicitly migrate SPEC_V1 to V3 semantics

local_semantic_ref.meaning: An identity resolved only inside an already pinned immutable canonical/specification artifact or registry closure. It is not an external locator.
local_semantic_ref.rule: Local semantic refs are safe only because the containing artifact/registry closure is immutable and uniquely selected. They MUST NOT silently escape to a mutable external lookup namespace.

interpretation_provenance_ref.meaning: A reference whose resolved content can change validation, interpretation, inheritance, readiness or historical reconstruction.
examples: external NodeTypes/Rulesets registry dependency when not embedded
interpretation_provenance_ref.rule: The same reference value MUST always resolve to the same content.

runtime_or_domain_ref.meaning: A domain/runtime reference whose mutability is governed by its own semantic contract and which is not automatically evaluation provenance.
runtime_or_domain_ref.immutable_external_resolution_required: only when another contract elevates it into interpretation provenance

evaluation_dependency_closure.principle: Immutable specification provenance applies to the full transitive interpretation/evaluation dependency closure, not only to the root specification_ref.
closure_members: NodeTypes registry content used by evaluation
Rulesets registry content used by evaluation
CCF/format/schema contract content used to interpret the artifacts
validation contract content used to validate the artifacts
any other external contract whose resolved content can change model validity or readiness
evaluation_dependency_closure.dependency_rule: Every closure member MUST either be embedded in an immutable parent artifact or be reached through an immutable-resolution interpretation_provenance_ref.
evaluation_dependency_closure.transitive_rule: If a closure member itself references another interpretation dependency, the same rule applies recursively.
forbidden: immutable root manifest containing a mutable NodeTypes pointer
immutable root manifest containing a mutable Rulesets pointer
immutable root manifest selecting a validation contract through a moving alias
CCF/format semantics resolved through latest/current/active
any transitive interpretation dependency changing while the root provenance reference stays unchanged
evaluation_dependency_closure.not_applied_automatically_to: runtime/domain references that do not participate in interpretation, validation or readiness

validation_contract_resolution.principle: The mapping from an artifact's version-scoped validation dispatch identity to validation-contract content MUST itself be immutable.
allowed_resolution_models: immutable validation-contract artifact identity + immutable revision/version
